title: Employers' Recognition of Hospitalisation Leave Issued by Community Hospitals
what_it_is: Employers' Recognition of Hospitalisation Leave Issued by Community Hospitals

sections.label: Community hospital leave recognition
sections.summary: Acute hospital hospitalisation leave stays valid under the Employment Act, and MOM intends to update the approved institutions list to include community hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Hospitalisation leave certified by a doctor from an acute hospital remains valid under the Employment Act (EA), even if the patient is subsequently transferred to a community hospital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Hospitalisation leave issued for patients directly admitted to a community hospital should be recognised under the EA, similar to stays in other public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, we understand that only a very small proportion of community hospital patients are directly admitted, that is, admitted without being referred by an acute hospital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Currently, the EA does not name the community hospitals as among the list of approved medical institutions for certifying hospitalisation leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) intends to work with the Ministry of Health (MOH) to update this list and will consult the tripartite partners before finalising it.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The review is ongoing and when we are ready, we will update Members.

sections.label: Recognised medical certificates for sick leave
sections.summary: MCs from Government medical officers or company-approved practitioners registered under the Medical Registration Act are recognised for paid sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: One part of it is that if it is issued by a Government medical officer, it will be recognised for the purposes of paid sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Alternatively, if the medical practitioner is registered under the Medical Registration Act and is part of a panel of company-approved practitioners, then the MCs are also recognised for paid sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, in the case of the Primary Care Network, if it falls into these two categories, then the answer is yes.
